Monte Carlo simulations allowed us to separate these effects Shifting judgments to ends of the scale did inflate JOL accuracy somewhat The bulk of the delayed-JOL effect, however, resulted from increases in calibration We conclude that the delayed-JOL effect reflects true metamemory improvement.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1111\/j.1467-9280.1997.tb00445.x","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2006,4,7]],"date-time":"2006-04-07T19:46:17Z","timestamp":1144439177000},"page":"318-321","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":33,"title":["Judgments of Learning at Delays: Shifts in Response Patterns or Increased Metamemory Accuracy?"],"prefix":"10.1177","volume":"8","author":[{"suffix":"III","given":"Charles A.","family":"Weaver","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"name":"Baylor University"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"William L.","family":"Kelemen","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[{"name":"Baylor University"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"member":"179","published-online":{"date-parts":[[1997,7,1]]},"reference":[{"key":"bibr1-j.1467-9280.1997.tb00445.x","doi-asserted-by":"publisher","DOI":"10.2307\/1423169"},{"key":"bibr2-j.1467-9280.1997.tb00445.x","doi-asserted-by":"publisher","DOI":"10.3758\/BF03210921"},{"key":"bibr3-j.1467-9280.1997.tb00445.x","doi-asserted-by":"publisher","DOI":"10.1006\/jmla.1994.1026"},{"key":"bibr4-j.1467-9280.1997.tb00445.x","unstructured":"Kelemen W.
